question: What is the name of ISRO's mission launched in January 2024 to study the polarisation of cosmic X-rays?
solution:
The correct answer is __**XPoSat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **XPoSat** is an acronym for the **X-ray Polarimeter Satellite**, launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** in **January 2024**.
 
• The mission is aimed at studying the **polarisation of cosmic X-rays**. Polarisation refers to the orientation of the electromagnetic waves, and understanding this helps to decipher celestial phenomena.
 
• XPoSat is India’s **first dedicated polarimetry mission**, designed to provide insights into **high-energy astrophysical phenomena** such as black holes, neutron stars, and pulsars. *Hence, XPoSat is the correct answer.*
 
• The satellite is equipped with the **Polarimeter instrument** to measure the degree and angle of polarisation of X-rays from various celestial sources.
 
• It aims to explore the **role of magnetic fields** and their interaction with high-energy particles in the universe. *This makes it a unique mission for space exploration.*
 
• The mission will contribute to the global database for astrophysics and enhance India’s capability in space science.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About XPoSat:**

 
 
• **XPoSat** will carry two scientific payloads: the primary **Polarimeter** and a secondary payload for monitoring particle flux.
 
• The **Polarimeter** will measure the polarisation of X-rays in a specific energy range to study celestial objects, while the secondary payload will observe the particle environment around Earth.
 
 
 
• **Significance of XPoSat:**
 
 
• It will help investigate **extreme physical environments** such as regions near black holes and neutron stars.
 
• The data collected will enhance our understanding of high-energy processes, magnetic fields, and particle acceleration mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Missions:**
 
 
• **Aditya-L1:** Another ISRO mission, launched earlier, studies the Sun's corona, solar radiation, and solar wind.
 
• **RISAT-1:** A radar imaging satellite focused on Earth observation for agricultural and disaster management applications.
 
• **AstroSat:** India’s first multi-wavelength space observatory, launched in 2015, which observes celestial sources in X-ray, UV, and optical wavelengths.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Why Polarisation is Important:**

 
 
• Polarisation measurements can reveal **hidden details about the structure, environment, and emission mechanisms** of celestial objects.
 
• It helps astrophysicists understand the behavior of **light and radiation** in high-energy environments.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• The success of XPoSat could pave the way for more advanced missions focused on polarimetry.
 
• It will strengthen India’s position in **space science** and provide valuable contributions to international collaborations in astrophysics.
